newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia state-owned banks complete restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia state-owned banks complete restructuring.

text.p: The Bank of Slovenia said on Friday the country's first and third largest state-owned banks, Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB) and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor, (NKBM) had successfully completed their rehabilitation process.
"The council of the Central Bank yesterday established that the two banks fulfil conditions to end the rehabilitation," Bank of Slovenia Governor France Arhar told a news conference.
Both banks, their balance sheets tainted by problem loans to former public sector enterprises, entered the programme in 1993. The restructuring was managed by the state Bank Rehabilitation Agency.
The government took over most of the two bank's non-performing assets, the majority of which stemmed from before 1991 when Slovenia gained independence from the former Yugoslavia.
The central bank said the two banks would now have to form new controlling and managing boards within 30 days of receiving the central bank's resolution, which was expected to be posted on Friday.
NLB's market share in Slovenia is 28 percent, while NKBM has an 11.5 percent share.
The government plans to privatise both banks at some point in the future but declined to detail a timeframe.
